title: Jetstar to Charge Passengers for Overhead Locker Access Starting February 2027
excerpt: Qantas's budget subsidiary will require travelers to purchase a Priority Carry-on add-on to stow bags in overhead bins, joining a global shift toward unbundled airfares.
body:
• Jetstar, Qantas's low-cost arm, will charge passengers A$25 to A$52 per flight for overhead locker access starting February 2027
  • Base fares will include only one small under-seat bag such as a backpack or laptop bag at no extra cost
  • The "Priority Carry-on" add-on removes the previous 7 kg weight limit and includes early boarding access
  • The policy aligns Jetstar with global budget carriers including Ryanair, Wizz Air, and Spirit Airlines that already charge for overhead bin space

What's Changing

Australian budget carrier Jetstar will require passengers to pay extra for overhead locker access from February 2027, the airline announced on Tuesday, overhauling its carry-on baggage policy in a move that drew immediate criticism from consumer groups.

Under the new rules, base fares will include only one bag small enough to fit under the seat — a backpack, handbag, or laptop bag. Passengers who want to stow a larger bag in the overhead locker will need to purchase a "Priority Carry-on" add-on, priced between A$25 and A$52 ($18 and $37) depending on the route, according to examples provided by the airline.

The add-on also removes the previous 7 kg weight limit on carry-on luggage and includes early boarding access.

Why Jetstar Says It's Necessary

Jetstar CEO Stephanie Tully said the change followed extensive customer and crew research that identified two persistent pain points: gate weigh-ins and competition for overhead locker space.

"You only pay for what you need — travelling with less means paying less, and you can always add more if you need."

— Stephanie Tully, Jetstar CEO

Tully said the new model would improve on-time departure performance by streamlining the boarding process, adding the changes were consistent with the airline's low-fares philosophy. The airline framed the move as a net benefit for passengers who travel light, arguing they would no longer subsidize overhead space used by others.

Global Trend in Unbundled Fares

The policy brings Jetstar in line with several low-cost carriers globally. European budget airlines Ryanair and Wizz Air already charge for overhead bin access, as do U.S. carriers Frontier and Spirit Airlines. Fees for baggage, seat selection, and priority boarding account for a growing share of revenue at budget carriers worldwide.

Consumer groups have long criticized the unbundling model, arguing that advertised base fares do not reflect the true cost of travel. Australia's Competition and Consumer Commission has previously examined whether ancillary fee structures could constitute misleading pricing, though it has not taken enforcement action against carry-on surcharges specifically.

What It Means for Travelers

For passengers flying Jetstar's popular domestic routes between Sydney, Melbourne, and Brisbane, the change means a cabin bag that currently flies free will soon require an add-on purchase. International travelers on Jetstar's Asia-Pacific network face similar charges, though exact pricing varies by route.

The new policy takes effect on Jetstar Airways (JQ) flights from February 2, 2027. Passengers who exceed their allowance at the gate without the add-on face excess carry-on fees of A$125 on domestic flights and up to A$175 on international routes — unchanged from current rates.

Jetstar, which operates as the low-cost subsidiary of Qantas, carried more than 30 million passengers in fiscal year 2025. Parent company Qantas has not indicated any similar changes to its own carry-on policy.
